###############################################################################
# School District Cost Model Explorer (Shiny)
#
# Walks through cost-behavior modeling for a school district -- fixed vs.
# variable costs and step costs -- via four tabs: Background, Elementary,
# High School, and District, each simulating staffing/building costs from
# detailed rules about how elementary, middle, and high schools are staffed.
#
# Cost rates (used throughout):
#   Supplies: $1,000/student, fully variable, no capacity constraint
#   Teachers: $80,000/teacher
#   Schools:  $1,500,000/school
#
# To run: open this file in RStudio and click "Run App" (requires the
# shiny, ggplot2, data.table, and scales packages).
###############################################################################

library(shiny)
library(ggplot2)
library(data.table)
library(scales)

# Forces R to always print numbers in plain fixed notation (e.g. 1500000,
# not 1.5e+06) everywhere in this app -- axis labels, dollar figures, and
# any other formatted number -- regardless of how large or small it is.
options(scipen = 999)

# ---- Cost rates -------------------------------------------------------------
teacher_capacity <- 25 # students per elementary classroom / per MS-HS section
supply_rate <- 1000 # $/student, fully variable
teacher_cost <- 80000 # $/teacher
school_cost <- 1500000 # $/school
district_mc_max_n <- 20000 # max district enrollment traced on the "6. Modeling Choices: District" tab

# Michigan Ross brand palette. Ross's confirmed brand colors are PMS 282 blue
# (#00274C) and PMS 7406 maize (#FFCB05); the style guide references a wider
# palette of "secondary accents" without publishing exact hex values, so
# "facility" and "model" below are Ross-blue/maize-family tints chosen to
# stay on-brand while giving enough separation for stacked/grouped charts.
palette_cb <- c(
  ink = "#00274C", # Ross Blue -- primary line/axis color
  highlow = "#FFCB05", # Ross Maize -- primary accent
  facility = "#5B87A6", # lighter Ross Blue tint -- secondary accent
  model = "#9A7B4F" # warm bronze/gold tint -- tertiary accent
)

# Callout text highlighted on the Elementary tab's chart: one entry for the
# building-expense jump, one for the School Supplies ramp, plus one for each
# of the three "waves" of teacher hiring (wave = which classroom, 1st/2nd/3rd,
# a hire is for). The supplies text is built from supply_rate (not a hard-
# coded dollar figure), so it always reflects the model's actual parameter.
elem_wave_text <- c(
  "building" = paste0(
    "Building expense occurs when the school enrolls its first student ",
    "and remains constant until the school reaches capacity."
  ),
  "supplies" = paste0(
    "Each student costs $",
    format(supply_rate, big.mark = ","),
    " in supplies. Thus, the school supplies cost increases smoothly ",
    "and linearly with enrollment."
  ),
  "1" = "A teacher is hired for each grade when the first student in that grade shows up.",
  "2" = paste0(
    "Once the first classroom in the grade fills, a second teacher needs to be ",
    "hired. These are somewhat staggered because students don't arrive across ",
    "all the grades completely evenly."
  ),
  "3" = paste0(
    "The third set of grade-school teachers are even more staggered as the ",
    "effects of uneven grade arrivals grow."
  )
)

# Callout text highlighted on the High School tab's chart: one entry
# explaining the vertical jumps (teachers hired in blocks of six), one
# explaining the horizontal steps (why their width varies).
high_wave_text <- c(
  "vertical" = paste0(
    "Teachers are always hired in groups of six -- one new teacher per ",
    "subject -- since every student takes all six subjects, so each ",
    "subject's section count crosses its own capacity threshold at the ",
    "same moment."
  ),
  "horizontal" = paste0(
    "The width of each flat step depends on the precise order students ",
    "arrive in -- whether the next student's grade already has room in an ",
    "existing section, or whether admitting them requires opening a brand ",
    "new section (and with it, another set of six teachers)."
  )
)

###############################################################################
# Core staffing/building rules
#
#   Elementary (K-5): self-contained classrooms. Each classroom holds up to
#   25 students and is staffed by 1 teacher. A school has room for at most 3
#   classrooms per grade (so an elementary school's true capacity, split
#   evenly across 6 grades, is 3 x 25 x 6 = 450 students).
#
#   Middle (6-8) and High (9-12): subject teachers. Every student takes all
#   6 subjects (English, Science, Math, Foreign Language, History, Specials).
#   Each subject section holds up to 25 students, and a section can only
#   include students from ONE grade (a 9th grade Math section can't also
#   seat 10th graders) -- but a teacher's 6 daily sections of a subject CAN
#   span different grades. So the number of sections a subject needs is the
#   SUM of each grade's own ceiling(enrollment/25), not a single ceiling of
#   the pooled enrollment, and teachers for that subject come in blocks of 6
#   sections (ceiling(sections/6)). A middle school has 36 classrooms and a
#   high school has 48; divided evenly across 6 subjects, that's a cap of 6
#   teachers/subject in a middle school and 8 teachers/subject in a high
#   school. If every grade were split perfectly evenly across the classes,
#   that cap works out to 900 students (middle) or 1,200 (high) -- but since
#   grades round up to sections separately, actual capacity is usually a bit
#   lower, the same way an elementary school rarely reaches its 450 max.
###############################################################################

grade_levels <- c("K", as.character(1:12)) # 13 grades, K-12
elem_grades <- c("K", "1", "2", "3", "4", "5")
middle_grades <- c("6", "7", "8")
high_grades <- c("9", "10", "11", "12")

elem_classrooms_per_grade_cap <- 3 # elementary: max classrooms per grade, per school

subjects <- c(
  "English",
  "Science",
  "Math",
  "Foreign Language",
  "History",
  "Specials"
)
teacher_classes_per_day <- 6 # a MS/HS teacher teaches 6 sections/day
teacher_student_capacity <- teacher_capacity * teacher_classes_per_day # 25 x 6 = 150

middle_classrooms_per_school <- 36
high_classrooms_per_school <- 48

# These are the THEORETICAL max capacities per school, reached only if every
# grade happened to divide perfectly evenly into 25-student sections. Kept
# around for that "theoretical maximum" narrative -- actual capacity, once
# each grade is rounded up to sections separately, is usually a bit lower.
middle_capacity_per_school <- floor(
  middle_classrooms_per_school / length(subjects)
) *
  teacher_student_capacity
high_capacity_per_school <- floor(
  high_classrooms_per_school / length(subjects)
) *
  teacher_student_capacity

middle_classrooms_per_subject <- floor(
  middle_classrooms_per_school / length(subjects)
) # 6
high_classrooms_per_subject <- floor(
  high_classrooms_per_school / length(subjects)
) # 8

# NOTE: the whole-district staffing snapshot (elem/mid/high enrollment,
# teachers, schools, and costs) is computed on the District tab by running
# the actual multi-building simulations (simulate_multi_elem() /
# simulate_multi_secondary()) rather than a closed-form approximation.

# ---- One-school, one-student-at-a-time simulations -------------------------
# Fills a SINGLE school from empty using an ordered sequence of grade draws
# (already filtered to the relevant grade band), and records the running cost
# after each student is admitted. A building expense hits at student 1. A
# teacher gets added only when the relevant classroom/subject count crosses
# another integer threshold. The elementary version stops the moment the next
# student in line belongs to a grade that has already filled its 3 classrooms
# (75 students) -- since that student would need a second building, this one
# school's story ends there, almost always short of the 450-student ceiling.
simulate_elem_school <- function(seq_grades) {
  grade_tally <- setNames(rep(0L, length(elem_grades)), elem_grades)
  classroom_tally <- setNames(rep(0L, length(elem_grades)), elem_grades)
  n_teachers <- 0L
  building_added <- FALSE
  running_cost <- 0

  n_max <- length(seq_grades)
  students <- integer(n_max)
  cum_cost <- numeric(n_max)
  cum_teach <- integer(n_max)
  n_admitted <- 0L
  capped_grade <- NA_character_

  # Every classroom a school adds is that grade's 1st, 2nd, or 3rd -- record
  # each hiring event's "wave" number (1/2/3) and the student count at which
  # it happened, so the UI can highlight where each wave of hiring clusters.
  event_students <- integer(0)
  event_wave <- integer(0)

  for (g in seq_grades) {
    if (grade_tally[[g]] >= elem_classrooms_per_grade_cap * teacher_capacity) {
      capped_grade <- g
      break
    }

    grade_tally[[g]] <- grade_tally[[g]] + 1L

    if (!building_added) {
      running_cost <- running_cost + school_cost
      building_added <- TRUE
    }

    new_classrooms <- ceiling(grade_tally[[g]] / teacher_capacity)
    if (new_classrooms > classroom_tally[[g]]) {
      added <- new_classrooms - classroom_tally[[g]]
      n_teachers <- n_teachers + added
      running_cost <- running_cost + added * teacher_cost
      classroom_tally[[g]] <- new_classrooms

      event_students <- c(event_students, n_admitted + 1L)
      event_wave <- c(event_wave, new_classrooms)
    }

    running_cost <- running_cost + supply_rate

    n_admitted <- n_admitted + 1L
    students[n_admitted] <- n_admitted
    cum_cost[n_admitted] <- running_cost
    cum_teach[n_admitted] <- n_teachers
  }

  list(
    trace = data.table(
      students = students[seq_len(n_admitted)],
      total_cost = cum_cost[seq_len(n_admitted)],
      teachers = cum_teach[seq_len(n_admitted)]
    ),
    grade_tally_final = grade_tally,
    capped_grade = capped_grade,
    events = data.table(students = event_students, wave = event_wave)
  )
}

# High school version: every student takes all 6 subjects, but a section
# can't mix grades -- a 9th grade Math section can't also seat 10th graders.
# So the sections a subject needs is the SUM of each grade's own
# ceiling(enrollment/25), and teachers for that subject arrive in blocks of
# 6 sections. All 6 subjects have identical demand (every student takes all
# of them), so they all hit the school's 8-teacher-per-subject ceiling at
# the same moment -- once admitting the next student would push the
# sections-per-subject total past 48 (8 teachers x 6 sections), the school
# stops admitting, almost always short of the 1,200-student theoretical max.
simulate_high_school <- function(seq_grades) {
  grade_tally <- setNames(rep(0L, length(high_grades)), high_grades)
  max_sections_per_subject <- high_classrooms_per_subject *
    teacher_classes_per_day # 48

  sections_per_subject <- 0L
  teachers_per_subject <- 0L
  n_teachers <- 0L
  building_added <- FALSE
  running_cost <- 0

  n_max <- length(seq_grades)
  students <- integer(n_max)
  cum_cost <- numeric(n_max)
  cum_teach <- integer(n_max)
  n_admitted <- 0L
  capped <- FALSE
  capped_grade <- NA_character_

  for (g in seq_grades) {
    old_grade_sections <- ceiling(grade_tally[[g]] / teacher_capacity)
    new_grade_sections <- ceiling((grade_tally[[g]] + 1L) / teacher_capacity)
    new_sections_per_subject <- sections_per_subject +
      (new_grade_sections - old_grade_sections)

    if (new_sections_per_subject > max_sections_per_subject) {
      capped <- TRUE
      capped_grade <- g
      break
    }

    grade_tally[[g]] <- grade_tally[[g]] + 1L
    sections_per_subject <- new_sections_per_subject

    if (!building_added) {
      running_cost <- running_cost + school_cost
      building_added <- TRUE
    }

    new_tps <- ceiling(sections_per_subject / teacher_classes_per_day)
    if (new_tps > teachers_per_subject) {
      added_total <- (new_tps - teachers_per_subject) * length(subjects)
      n_teachers <- n_teachers + added_total
      running_cost <- running_cost + added_total * teacher_cost
      teachers_per_subject <- new_tps
    }

    running_cost <- running_cost + supply_rate

    n_admitted <- n_admitted + 1L
    students[n_admitted] <- n_admitted
    cum_cost[n_admitted] <- running_cost
    cum_teach[n_admitted] <- n_teachers
  }

  list(
    trace = data.table(
      students = students[seq_len(n_admitted)],
      total_cost = cum_cost[seq_len(n_admitted)],
      teachers = cum_teach[seq_len(n_admitted)]
    ),
    capped = capped,
    capped_grade = capped_grade
  )
}

# ---- Multi-building simulations ---------------------------------------------
# These extend the single-school simulations above to a WHOLE grade band
# (potentially several school buildings): instead of stopping once the
# current building's capacity is hit, they open a fresh building and keep
# admitting the same ordered sequence of students there. This is a real,
# order-respecting bin-packing of students into buildings -- not a closed-
# form approximation -- so it correctly captures rounding waste from
# students being split across multiple buildings. Each returns a CUMULATIVE
# districtwide trace, one row per student in that band, in arrival order.

simulate_multi_elem <- function(seq_grades) {
  n_max <- length(seq_grades)
  if (n_max == 0) {
    return(data.table(
      students = integer(0),
      total_cost = numeric(0),
      teachers = integer(0),
      schools = integer(0)
    ))
  }

  grade_tally <- setNames(rep(0L, length(elem_grades)), elem_grades)
  classroom_tally <- setNames(rep(0L, length(elem_grades)), elem_grades)

  total_teachers <- 0L
  total_schools <- 0L
  running_cost <- 0

  students <- integer(n_max)
  cum_cost <- numeric(n_max)
  cum_teach <- integer(n_max)
  cum_sch <- integer(n_max)

  for (i in seq_len(n_max)) {
    g <- seq_grades[i]

    # No building open yet, or this grade has already filled its 3
    # classrooms in the CURRENT building -- open a fresh elementary school
    # (its own 6 grades, all empty) and admit this student there instead.
    if (
      total_schools == 0L ||
        grade_tally[[g]] >= elem_classrooms_per_grade_cap * teacher_capacity
    ) {
      grade_tally <- setNames(rep(0L, length(elem_grades)), elem_grades)
      classroom_tally <- setNames(rep(0L, length(elem_grades)), elem_grades)
      total_schools <- total_schools + 1L
      running_cost <- running_cost + school_cost
    }

    grade_tally[[g]] <- grade_tally[[g]] + 1L

    new_classrooms <- ceiling(grade_tally[[g]] / teacher_capacity)
    if (new_classrooms > classroom_tally[[g]]) {
      added <- new_classrooms - classroom_tally[[g]]
      total_teachers <- total_teachers + added
      running_cost <- running_cost + added * teacher_cost
      classroom_tally[[g]] <- new_classrooms
    }

    running_cost <- running_cost + supply_rate

    students[i] <- i
    cum_cost[i] <- running_cost
    cum_teach[i] <- total_teachers
    cum_sch[i] <- total_schools
  }

  data.table(
    students = students,
    total_cost = cum_cost,
    teachers = cum_teach,
    schools = cum_sch
  )
}

# Generic middle/high version -- classrooms_per_school (36 or 48) and the
# relevant grade band are passed in, since middle and high schools follow
# the identical subject-teacher rule, just with different building sizes.
simulate_multi_secondary <- function(
  seq_grades,
  secondary_grades,
  classrooms_per_school
) {
  n_max <- length(seq_grades)
  if (n_max == 0) {
    return(data.table(
      students = integer(0),
      total_cost = numeric(0),
      teachers = integer(0),
      schools = integer(0)
    ))
  }

  classrooms_per_subject <- floor(classrooms_per_school / length(subjects))
  max_sections_per_subject <- classrooms_per_subject * teacher_classes_per_day

  grade_tally <- setNames(rep(0L, length(secondary_grades)), secondary_grades)
  sections_per_subject <- 0L
  teachers_per_subject <- 0L

  total_teachers <- 0L
  total_schools <- 0L
  running_cost <- 0

  students <- integer(n_max)
  cum_cost <- numeric(n_max)
  cum_teach <- integer(n_max)
  cum_sch <- integer(n_max)

  for (i in seq_len(n_max)) {
    g <- seq_grades[i]

    old_g_sections <- ceiling(grade_tally[[g]] / teacher_capacity)
    new_g_sections <- ceiling((grade_tally[[g]] + 1L) / teacher_capacity)
    would_be <- sections_per_subject + (new_g_sections - old_g_sections)

    # No building open yet, or this student would push some subject's
    # section count past capacity in the CURRENT building -- open a fresh
    # one (a whole new set of subject-teacher slots) and admit there.
    if (total_schools == 0L || would_be > max_sections_per_subject) {
      grade_tally <- setNames(
        rep(0L, length(secondary_grades)),
        secondary_grades
      )
      sections_per_subject <- 0L
      teachers_per_subject <- 0L
      total_schools <- total_schools + 1L
      running_cost <- running_cost + school_cost
      would_be <- 1L # this student is grade g's first in the fresh building
    }

    grade_tally[[g]] <- grade_tally[[g]] + 1L
    sections_per_subject <- would_be

    new_tps <- ceiling(sections_per_subject / teacher_classes_per_day)
    if (new_tps > teachers_per_subject) {
      added <- (new_tps - teachers_per_subject) * length(subjects)
      total_teachers <- total_teachers + added
      running_cost <- running_cost + added * teacher_cost
      teachers_per_subject <- new_tps
    }

    running_cost <- running_cost + supply_rate

    students[i] <- i
    cum_cost[i] <- running_cost
    cum_teach[i] <- total_teachers
    cum_sch[i] <- total_schools
  }

  data.table(
    students = students,
    total_cost = cum_cost,
    teachers = cum_teach,
    schools = cum_sch
  )
}

# Vectorized helper for the District tab: given one band's
# multi-building trace (indexed 1..n by that band's OWN arrival order) and,
# for every overall district step, how many of that band's students have
# arrived so far (pos_vec), look up that band's teachers/schools at every
# overall step in one shot. A position of 0 (no students from this band yet)
# maps to 0 rather than being dropped, which is how R would normally treat a
# 0 index.
band_lookup <- function(trace, pos_vec, col) {
  out <- integer(length(pos_vec))
  hit <- pos_vec > 0
  out[hit] <- trace[[col]][pos_vec[hit]]
  out
}

# Same idea as band_lookup() above, but for a single scalar index -- used on
# the Modeling Choices tabs, where the "starting enrollment" and "change in
# enrollment" sliders now allow 0. R's normal vector indexing (vec[0])
# silently returns an empty (length-0) vector rather than an error, which
# then breaks every downstream calculation that reads it; this maps a 0 (or
# negative) index to a literal 0 instead, matching "$0 spent before any
# students have arrived."
idx_or_zero <- function(vec, n) if (n <= 0) 0 else vec[n]

###############################################################################
# "7. Assessing Model Fit" tab support.
#
# For a fixed seed (1) and district enrollment (10,000), what does a
# "typical" filled school of each type actually look like? Computed once,
# here, at load time (rather than as a reactive), since it's a fixed
# illustrative baseline for the tab's narrative, not something the user
# adjusts. simulate_multi_elem()/simulate_multi_secondary() already run a
# real, order-respecting bin-packing of students into buildings -- not a
# closed-form approximation -- so a "filled" building's actual population
# can land a bit under its theoretical max (450/900/1,200) depending on how
# enrollment happened to split across grades.
###############################################################################

model_fit_seed <- 1
model_fit_n <- 10000

set.seed(model_fit_seed)
model_fit_draws <- sample(grade_levels, model_fit_n, replace = TRUE)

model_fit_elem_trace <- simulate_multi_elem(model_fit_draws[
  model_fit_draws %in% elem_grades
])
model_fit_mid_trace <- simulate_multi_secondary(
  model_fit_draws[model_fit_draws %in% middle_grades],
  middle_grades,
  middle_classrooms_per_school
)
model_fit_high_trace <- simulate_multi_secondary(
  model_fit_draws[model_fit_draws %in% high_grades],
  high_grades,
  high_classrooms_per_school
)

# Average population and average teacher count across every CLOSED building
# in a band's trace -- i.e. every school except the last one, which is still
# in the process of filling up and hasn't reached capacity yet.
filled_school_stats <- function(trace) {
  n <- nrow(trace)
  if (n == 0) {
    return(list(
      avg_students = NA_real_,
      avg_teachers = NA_real_,
      n_filled = 0L
    ))
  }

  starts <- which(diff(c(0L, trace$schools)) > 0)
  ends <- c(starts[-1] - 1L, n)
  pop <- ends - starts + 1L
  teach_before <- c(0L, trace$teachers[starts[-1] - 1L])
  teachers <- trace$teachers[ends] - teach_before

  n_schools <- length(starts)
  if (n_schools < 2) {
    return(list(
      avg_students = NA_real_,
      avg_teachers = NA_real_,
      n_filled = 0L
    ))
  }

  filled_idx <- seq_len(n_schools - 1)
  list(
    avg_students = mean(pop[filled_idx]),
    avg_teachers = mean(teachers[filled_idx]),
    n_filled = length(filled_idx)
  )
}

model_fit_elem_stats <- filled_school_stats(model_fit_elem_trace)
model_fit_mid_stats <- filled_school_stats(model_fit_mid_trace)
model_fit_high_stats <- filled_school_stats(model_fit_high_trace)

###############################################################################
# The "overfit" model itself: every cost (Building, Teachers, Supplies) is
# treated as fully Variable, but Building and Teacher capacities use the
# CALCULATED averages from the actual filled schools above (rather than the
# textbook 450/900/1,200-student, 25-student-per-teacher assumptions used
# elsewhere in the app). Since everything is Variable, the model collapses
# to a single blended $/student rate per band -- exactly like choosing
# "Variable" for every cost on tabs 5/6 -- weighted by each band's share of
# the district's 13 grade levels, since that's the model's best guess at how
# any given batch of new students will split across elementary/middle/high.
###############################################################################

model_fit_elem_teacher_capacity <- model_fit_elem_stats$avg_students /
  model_fit_elem_stats$avg_teachers
model_fit_mid_teacher_capacity <- model_fit_mid_stats$avg_students /
  model_fit_mid_stats$avg_teachers
model_fit_high_teacher_capacity <- model_fit_high_stats$avg_students /
  model_fit_high_stats$avg_teachers

model_fit_elem_rate <- school_cost /
  model_fit_elem_stats$avg_students +
  teacher_cost / model_fit_elem_teacher_capacity +
  supply_rate
model_fit_mid_rate <- school_cost /
  model_fit_mid_stats$avg_students +
  teacher_cost / model_fit_mid_teacher_capacity +
  supply_rate
model_fit_high_rate <- school_cost /
  model_fit_high_stats$avg_students +
  teacher_cost / model_fit_high_teacher_capacity +
  supply_rate

model_fit_elem_frac <- length(elem_grades) / length(grade_levels)
model_fit_mid_frac <- length(middle_grades) / length(grade_levels)
model_fit_high_frac <- length(high_grades) / length(grade_levels)

model_fit_blended_rate <- model_fit_elem_frac *
  model_fit_elem_rate +
  model_fit_mid_frac * model_fit_mid_rate +
  model_fit_high_frac * model_fit_high_rate

model_fit_growth_scenarios <- c(100, 1000, 3000, 6000)
model_fit_scenario_labels <- paste0(
  "+",
  format(model_fit_growth_scenarios, big.mark = ",", trim = TRUE),
  " students"
)

###############################################################################
# Building- and Teacher-expense versions of the "overfit" model: isolate
# just the Building (and separately, Teacher) cost component of the
# blended linear model (school_cost / avg. capacity, and teacher_cost /
# avg. students-per-teacher, weighted by each band's share of the
# district's grade levels, using seed 1's calculated capacities from
# above), and compare each predicted INCREASE for a given growth scenario
# against the ACTUAL increase realized across 1,000 independently-
# simulated growth patterns.
#
# The first 10,000 students always arrive in seed 2's order
# (model_fit_mc_base_draws) -- a fixed, known starting point that's
# independent of the seed-1 draw the model's capacities were built from.
# For each of 1,000 seeds (3-1002), only the INCREMENTAL 100/1,000/3,000/
# 5,000 students on top of those first 10,000 are independently simulated,
# so each seed represents one plausible way the district's NEXT batch of
# students could arrive, continuing on from the same known starting point.
# The increase in expense from 10,000 to each target is therefore the
# marginal cost of that seed's own particular growth pattern layered onto
# the shared base -- across 1,000 seeds it traces out a real distribution
# of plausible outcomes to compare the model's single predicted number
# against.
#
# Building and Teacher costs are computed together in a single pass per
# seed (since both come from the same underlying school/teacher trace),
# to avoid doubling the most expensive thing this app computes at load
# time (1,000+ independent simulations). The user can't change any of its
# inputs from the UI -- so the result is cached to disk the first time it
# runs, keyed on the parameters that would actually change it, and reused
# (near-instantly) on every subsequent app launch until one of those
# parameters changes.
###############################################################################

model_fit_elem_building_rate <- school_cost / model_fit_elem_stats$avg_students
model_fit_mid_building_rate <- school_cost / model_fit_mid_stats$avg_students
model_fit_high_building_rate <- school_cost / model_fit_high_stats$avg_students

model_fit_blended_building_rate <- model_fit_elem_frac *
  model_fit_elem_building_rate +

model_fit_component_costs_from_draws <- function(draws, targets) {
  ind <- sapply(grade_levels, function(g) as.integer(draws == g))
  cum_counts <- apply(ind, 2, cumsum)
  colnames(cum_counts) <- grade_levels

  elem_pos_vec <- rowSums(cum_counts[, elem_grades, drop = FALSE])
  mid_pos_vec <- rowSums(cum_counts[, middle_grades, drop = FALSE])
  high_pos_vec <- rowSums(cum_counts[, high_grades, drop = FALSE])

  elem_trace <- simulate_multi_elem(draws[draws %in% elem_grades])
  mid_trace <- simulate_multi_secondary(
    draws[draws %in% middle_grades],
    middle_grades,
    middle_classrooms_per_school
  )
  high_trace <- simulate_multi_secondary(
    draws[draws %in% high_grades],
    high_grades,
    high_classrooms_per_school
  )

  total_schools_vec <- band_lookup(elem_trace, elem_pos_vec, "schools") +
    band_lookup(mid_trace, mid_pos_vec, "schools") +
    band_lookup(high_trace, high_pos_vec, "schools")
  total_teachers_vec <- band_lookup(elem_trace, elem_pos_vec, "teachers") +
    band_lookup(mid_trace, mid_pos_vec, "teachers") +
    band_lookup(high_trace, high_pos_vec, "teachers")

  list(
    building = (total_schools_vec * school_cost)[targets],
    teacher = (total_teachers_vec * teacher_cost)[targets]
  )
}

# Monte Carlo seeds (3-1002): the first 10,000 students are always
# model_fit_mc_base_draws (seed 2, fixed); only the incremental students on
# top of that shared base are drawn from the given tail_seed.
model_fit_component_cost_at_tail <- function(tail_seed, targets) {
  max_n <- max(targets)
  tail_n <- max_n - model_fit_n
  set.seed(tail_seed)
  tail_draws <- if (tail_n > 0) {
    sample(grade_levels, tail_n, replace = TRUE)
  } else {
    character(0)
  }
  draws <- c(model_fit_mc_base_draws, tail_draws)
  model_fit_component_costs_from_draws(draws, targets)
}

  tabPanel(

    fluidPage(

      # Placeholder for an embedded video -- swap the contents of this div

# ---- Server -------------------------------------------------------------------
server <- function(input, output, session) {
  ##############################################################################
  # "7. Assessing Model Fit" tab: a standalone 1x4 (growth scenario) row of

  # (model_fit_building_hist_data / model_fit_building_pred_lines,

        fill = palette_cb[["ink"]],

      labs(
        title = "Actual Additional Building Expense Across 1,000 Random Draws (Seeds 3-1002) vs. Modeled Prediction",

      theme_minimal(base_size = 13) +
      theme(
        axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 30, hjust = 1),
        plot.margin = margin(t = 8, r = 16, b = 8, l = 8)
      )
  })

  # Click-to-explain callout for the standalone Building-expense 1x4: each
  # panel is one growth scenario (facet_wrap(~ scenario) with a single
  # facet variable), so Shiny's click event reports which one was clicked
  # via panelvar1 -- same technique used for the highlighted ovals on the
  # Elementary/High School/District tabs, just without oval hit-testing
  # since here the whole panel is clickable.
  output$modelFitBuildingCallout <- renderUI({
    click <- input$modelFitBuildingClick
    panel <- click$panelvar1
    if (is.null(panel)) {
      return(NULL)
    }

    msg <- switch(
      panel,
      "+100 students" = paste0(
        "In none of the simulations did we need to add another school. As a result, ",
        "building expense always overestimates our cost increase by $",
        format(round(model_fit_blended_building_rate * 100), big.mark = ","),
        " (the blended rate times 100 students)."
      ),
      "+1,000 students" = paste0(
        "In all of the simulations, we needed to add a single elementary school. Again, ",
        "treating building expense as variable considerably overestimates the additional ",
        "costs we face from the increased enrollment."
      ),
      "+3,000 students" = paste0(
        "At this level of additions, we see some divergence in our simulations based on ",
        "arrival patterns. In almost all scenarios, we needed to open 5 schools. However, ",
        "for a handful of scenarios, we needed to open 6. Treating building expense as ",
        "fully variable is roughly equivalent to opening approximately 5.1 schools. We ",
        "can't open 0.1 of a school, but this number at least balances, to some extent, ",
        "the idea that sometimes we'll have to open 5 and sometimes we'll have to open 6. ",
        "Depending on how these numbers are going to be used, it may be useful to have the ",
        "expense reflect this remote possibility or it may be better to estimate 5 schools, ",
        "given that's the overwhelmingly likely scenario."
      ),
      "+6,000 students" = paste0(
        "When we increase enrollment by 6,000 students, in 1/8 of the simulations we ",
        "added 10 schools. In 7/8 of the simulations, we added 11. Using a variable cost ",
        "splits the difference almost proportionally."
      ),
      NULL
    )
    if (is.null(msg)) {
      return(NULL)
    }

    div(
      class = "situation-card",
      style = "font-size: 13px; line-height: 1.5;",
      tags$strong(sub("students$", "Students", panel)),
      " ",
      msg
    )
  })

  ##############################################################################
  # "7. Assessing Model Fit" tab: a second 1x4 (growth scenario) row of
  # histograms of the Monte Carlo actual Teacher expense increases
  # (model_fit_teacher_hist_data / model_fit_teacher_pred_lines,
  # precomputed once at load time above) against the variable-cost model's
  # single predicted Teacher expense increase for each growth scenario.
  # Filled gold (palette_cb[["highlow"]]), matching "Teacher salaries" on
  # the other tabs.
  ##############################################################################

  output$modelFitHistograms <- renderPlot({
    ggplot(model_fit_teacher_hist_data, aes(x = increase)) +
      geom_histogram(
        bins = 30,
        fill = palette_cb[["highlow"]],
        color = palette_cb[["ink"]],
        alpha = 0.6,
        linewidth = 0.3
      ) +
      geom_vline(
        data = model_fit_teacher_pred_lines,
        aes(xintercept = predicted),
        color = "#D7263D",
        linewidth = 1,
        linetype = "dashed"
      ) +
      facet_wrap(~scenario, scales = "free", ncol = 4) +
      scale_x_continuous(labels = comma, expand = expansion(mult = 0.12)) +
      scale_y_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.12))) +
      labs(
        title = "Actual Additional Teacher Expense Across 1,000 Random Draws (Seeds 3-1002) vs. Modeled Prediction",
        subtitle = "Dashed red line = the variable-cost model's predicted increase in teacher expense",
        x = "Additional Teacher Expense ($)",
        y = "Count"
      ) +
      theme_minimal(base_size = 13) +
      theme(
        axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 30, hjust = 1),
        plot.margin = margin(t = 8, r = 16, b = 8, l = 8)
      )
  })

  # Click-to-explain callout for the Teacher-expense 1x4 -- same technique
  # as the Building-expense callout above (facet_wrap(~ scenario) reports
  # which panel was clicked via panelvar1).
  output$modelFitTeacherCallout <- renderUI({
    click <- input$modelFitTeacherClick
    panel <- click$panelvar1
    if (is.null(panel)) {
      return(NULL)
    }

    msg <- switch(
      panel,
      "+100 students" = paste0(
        "When adding 100 students, we rarely need to add teachers (<5% of the time). ",
        "However, treating teachers as fully variable results in an expected cost ",
        "increase of $",
        format(
          round(model_fit_teacher_predicted["+100 students"]),
          big.mark = ","
        ),
        " (~",
        round(model_fit_teacher_predicted["+100 students"] / teacher_cost, 1),
        " teachers) calculated using the blended rate."
      ),
      "+1,000 students" = paste0(
        "At an enrollment increase of 1,000 students, we see considerable divergence in ",
        "the number of teachers added. While the variable cost estimation is somewhat to ",
        "the high end of the possible cost increases, it is well within the realm of ",
        "possibilities."
      ),
      "+3,000 students" = "We see similar patterns as with +1,000 students.",
      "+6,000 students" = "The variable cost estimate is entirely reasonable.",
      NULL
    )
    if (is.null(msg)) {
      return(NULL)
    }

    div(
      class = "situation-card",
      style = "font-size: 13px; line-height: 1.5;",
      tags$strong(sub("students$", "Students", panel)),
      " ",
      msg
    )
  })

  ##############################################################################
  # "7. Assessing Model Fit" tab: the final discrete-step model ("Assembling
  # the Pieces" above) plotted against the district's TRUE total cost curve
  # for whichever seed is currently selected via the Random Seed control at
  # the bottom of this tab. Driven by its own trigger/seed reactiveVal pair
  # (same pattern as districtMCTrigger/districtMCSeedValue on tab 6) so it's
  # completely independent of the 1x4 histograms above -- those are
  # precomputed once at load time over a fixed bank of seeds, and this
  # Random Seed control does not touch them.
  ##############################################################################

  modelFitFinalTrigger <- reactiveVal(0)
  modelFitFinalSeedValue <- reactiveVal(1)

  observeEvent(input$generate_model_fit_final, {
    modelFitFinalSeedValue(input$rand_seed_model_fit)
    modelFitFinalTrigger(modelFitFinalTrigger() + 1)
  })

  modelFitFinalSim <- eventReactive(
    modelFitFinalTrigger(),
    {
      seed <- modelFitFinalSeedValue()
      max_n <- district_mc_max_n

      set.seed(seed)
      draws <- sample(grade_levels, max_n, replace = TRUE)

      ind <- sapply(grade_levels, function(g) as.integer(draws == g))
      cum_counts <- apply(ind, 2, cumsum)
      colnames(cum_counts) <- grade_levels

      elem_pos_vec <- rowSums(cum_counts[, elem_grades, drop = FALSE])
      mid_pos_vec <- rowSums(cum_counts[, middle_grades, drop = FALSE])
      high_pos_vec <- rowSums(cum_counts[, high_grades, drop = FALSE])

      elem_trace <- simulate_multi_elem(draws[draws %in% elem_grades])
      mid_trace <- simulate_multi_secondary(
        draws[draws %in% middle_grades],
        middle_grades,
        middle_classrooms_per_school
      )
      high_trace <- simulate_multi_secondary(
        draws[draws %in% high_grades],
        high_grades,
        high_classrooms_per_school
      )

      total_schools_vec <- band_lookup(elem_trace, elem_pos_vec, "schools") +
        band_lookup(mid_trace, mid_pos_vec, "schools") +
        band_lookup(high_trace, high_pos_vec, "schools")
      total_teachers_vec <- band_lookup(elem_trace, elem_pos_vec, "teachers") +
        band_lookup(mid_trace, mid_pos_vec, "teachers") +
        band_lookup(high_trace, high_pos_vec, "teachers")

      students <- seq_len(max_n)
      true_cost <- total_schools_vec *
        school_cost +
        total_teachers_vec * teacher_cost +
        students * supply_rate

      # The "Assembling the Pieces" model: discrete school buildings per band
      # (ceiling of enrollment over each band's fill threshold), plus fully
      # Variable teacher (blended calculated rate, not the standard $80,000/25)
      # and supply costs.
      modeled_cost <- school_cost *
        (ceiling(students / model_fit_elem_threshold) +
          ceiling(students / model_fit_mid_threshold) +
          ceiling(students / model_fit_high_threshold)) +
        (supply_rate + model_fit_blended_teacher_rate) * students

      data.table(
        students = students,
        true_cost = true_cost,
        modeled_cost = modeled_cost
      )
    },
    ignoreNULL = FALSE,
    ignoreInit = FALSE
  )

  output$modelFitFinalPlot <- renderPlot({
    sim <- modelFitFinalSim()

    view_range <- input$model_fit_final_view_range
    validate(need(
      !is.null(view_range) &&
        length(view_range) == 2 &&
        view_range[2] > view_range[1],
      "Widen the plot view range slider -- the minimum can't equal the maximum."
    ))
    view_lo <- max(0, view_range[1])
    view_hi <- min(nrow(sim), view_range[2])

    plot_data <- rbindlist(list(
      data.table(
        students = sim$students,
        cost = sim$true_cost,
        series = "True cost"
      ),
      data.table(
        students = sim$students,
        cost = sim$modeled_cost,
        series = "Final model"
      )
    ))
    plot_data[,
      series := factor(series, levels = c("True cost", "Final model"))
    ]

    visible_idx <- which(sim$students >= view_lo & sim$students <= view_hi)
    y_max_visible <- max(
      sim$true_cost[visible_idx],
      sim$modeled_cost[visible_idx]
    )

    ggplot(
      plot_data,
      aes(x = students, y = cost, color = series, linetype = series)
    ) +
      geom_line(linewidth = 0.8) +
      scale_color_manual(
        name = NULL,
        values = c("True cost" = palette_cb[["ink"]], "Final model" = "#D7263D")
      ) +
      scale_linetype_manual(
        name = NULL,
        values = c("True cost" = "solid", "Final model" = "dashed")
      ) +
      coord_cartesian(
        xlim = c(view_lo, view_hi),
        ylim = c(0, y_max_visible * 1.12)
      ) +
      scale_x_continuous(labels = comma) +
      scale_y_continuous(labels = comma) +
      labs(
        title = paste0(
          "Final Model vs. True District Cost, ",
          format(view_lo, big.mark = ","),
          "-",
          format(view_hi, big.mark = ","),
          " Students (Seed ",
          modelFitFinalSeedValue(),
          ")"
        ),
        x = "Students",
        y = "Total Cost ($)"
      ) +
      theme_minimal(base_size = 13) +
      theme(legend.position = "bottom")
  })

  # Kernel density of the model's error (Final model - True cost) at every
  # single enrollment level from 1 to district_mc_max_n (20,000 data
  # points), for whichever seed is currently selected. Reuses
  # modelFitFinalSim() -- the same simulation that drives the plot above --
  # so this always reflects the exact same draw, over its full range
  # (independent of the "Plot view" zoom slider, which only affects the
  # plot above).
  output$modelFitErrorDensity <- renderPlot({
    sim <- modelFitFinalSim()
    error_data <- data.table(error = sim$modeled_cost - sim$true_cost)

    ggplot(error_data, aes(x = error)) +
      geom_density(
        fill = "grey70",
        color = "grey30",
        alpha = 0.6,
        linewidth = 0.7
      ) +
      geom_vline(
        xintercept = 0,
        color = "grey20",
        linewidth = 1,
        linetype = "solid"
      ) +
      scale_x_continuous(labels = comma) +
      labs(
        title = paste0(
          "Distribution of Model Error, 1-",
          format(nrow(sim), big.mark = ","),
          " Students (Seed ",
          modelFitFinalSeedValue(),
          ")"
        ),
        subtitle = "Error = Final model cost - True cost (solid line = zero error)",
        x = "Error ($)",
        y = "Density"
      ) +
      theme_minimal(base_size = 13)
  })

  output$modelFitErrorSummary <- renderUI({
    sim <- modelFitFinalSim()
    error <- sim$modeled_cost - sim$true_cost

    p(
      style = "margin-top: 4px; margin-bottom: 16px;",
      strong("Mean error: "),
      paste0("$", format(round(mean(error)), big.mark = ",")),
      HTML("  |  "),
      strong("Median error: "),
      paste0("$", format(round(median(error)), big.mark = ",")),
      HTML("  |  "),
      strong("Std. dev.: "),
      paste0("$", format(round(sd(error)), big.mark = ","))
    )
  })

  ##############################################################################
  # Shared "current student body" parameters (used by the Elementary and
  # High School tabs)
  ##############################################################################

  # Shared "current student body" parameters. The Elementary and High
  # School tabs' Generate buttons both write into this one reactiveValues
  # object, and their random-seed fields are kept in sync with it.
  body_params <- reactiveValues(n = 5000, seed = 1)

  # The Elementary/High School tabs don't expose a student-count field at
  # all -- they always generate this many students in the background, which
  # is comfortably enough for both schools to run out of classroom capacity
  # well before this pool is exhausted, whatever the current seed's mix.
  elem_high_default_n <- 25000

  observeEvent(input$generate_body_elem, {
    body_params$n <- elem_high_default_n
    body_params$seed <- input$rand_seed_elem
  })
  observeEvent(input$generate_body_high, {
    body_params$n <- elem_high_default_n
    body_params$seed <- input$rand_seed_high
  })
  observeEvent(input$generate_body_high_mc, {
    body_params$n <- elem_high_default_n
    body_params$seed <- input$rand_seed_high_mc
  })

  # Puts every control on the "5. Modeling Choices: High School" tab back to
  # its original default, including the random seed, and re-triggers the
  # same body-generation the Refresh button would (so the plot/stats update
  # even if the seed was already 1 and wouldn't otherwise re-fire).
  observeEvent(input$mc_reset_defaults, {
    updateSliderInput(session, "mc_start", value = 725)
    updateSliderInput(session, "mc_delta", value = 50)
    updateNumericInput(session, "mc_school_cost", value = school_cost)
    updateNumericInput(session, "mc_supply_rate", value = supply_rate)
    updateNumericInput(session, "mc_teacher_cost", value = teacher_cost)
    updateNumericInput(session, "mc_teacher_capacity", value = teacher_capacity)
    updateRadioButtons(session, "mc_building_choice", selected = "Variable")
    updateRadioButtons(session, "mc_supplies_choice", selected = "Variable")
    updateRadioButtons(session, "mc_teacher_choice", selected = "Variable")
    updateNumericInput(session, "rand_seed_high_mc", value = 1)
    body_params$n <- elem_high_default_n
    body_params$seed <- 1
  })

  observeEvent(
    body_params$seed,
    {
      updateNumericInput(session, "rand_seed_elem", value = body_params$seed)
      updateNumericInput(session, "rand_seed_high", value = body_params$seed)
      updateNumericInput(session, "rand_seed_high_mc", value = body_params$seed)
    },
    ignoreInit = TRUE
  )

  # Keeps the "Change in enrollment" slider's own range in sync with the
  # starting enrollment, so the ending enrollment (start + delta) can never
  # be pushed below 0 or above the full enrollment the current high school
  # draw admits -- while still allowing decreases (negative delta) as well
  # as increases.
  observe({
    cap <- nrow(highSim()$trace)
    lo <- -input$mc_start
    hi <- max(lo, cap - input$mc_start)
    updateSliderInput(
      session,
      "mc_delta",
      min = lo,
      max = hi,
      value = min(max(input$mc_delta, lo), hi)
    )
  })

  # Shared district-wide random draw (ordered), rebuilt whenever body_params
  # changes. This is the single source of truth for the current student
  # body -- the Elementary and High School Cost Implications tabs both
  # read from it.
  studentDraws <- reactive({
    set.seed(body_params$seed)
    sample(grade_levels, body_params$n, replace = TRUE)
  })

  ##############################################################################
  # Elementary/High School Cost Implications tabs: fill one school from
  # empty, one student at a time, using the shared studentDraws() above.
  ##############################################################################

  elemSim <- reactive({
    simulate_elem_school(studentDraws()[studentDraws() %in% elem_grades])
  })

  # Geometry (in data coordinates) for the highlight ovals: one marking the
  # building-expense jump at student 1, plus three marking the "waves" of
  # teacher hiring -- wave 1 = every grade's 1st classroom, wave 2 = every
  # grade's 2nd, wave 3 = every grade's 3rd. Recomputed from the CURRENT
  # simulation, so the ovals track wherever those clusters actually land for
  # the active seed/draw. Each region also records which FACET PANEL it
  # belongs to, since building and teacher jumps now live in separate rows.
  elemWaveRegions <- reactive({
    result <- elemSim()
    sim <- result$trace
    ev <- result$events
    if (nrow(sim) == 0) {
      return(list())
    }

    teacher_cum <- sim$teachers * teacher_cost
    teacher_max <- max(teacher_cum)

    building_region <- list(
      key = "building",
      panel = "Building Expense",
      cx = 1,
      cy = school_cost / 2,
      rx = max(nrow(sim) * 0.03, 1.5),
      ry = school_cost / 2 * 1.15,
      label = elem_wave_text[["building"]]
    )

    # Supplies cost is a straight line (supply_rate per student), so the
    # oval just hugs a point partway along that ramp rather than a jump.
    supplies_max <- supply_rate * nrow(sim)
    sup_cx <- nrow(sim) * 0.6
    supplies_region <- list(
      key = "supplies",
      panel = "School Supplies",
      cx = sup_cx,
      cy = supply_rate * sup_cx,
      rx = max(nrow(sim) * 0.07, 3),
      ry = max(supplies_max * 0.09, 1),
      label = elem_wave_text[["supplies"]]
    )

    wave_regions <- if (nrow(ev) > 0) {
      Filter(
        Negate(is.null),
        lapply(1:3, function(w) {
          sub <- ev[wave == w]
          if (nrow(sub) == 0) {
            return(NULL)
          }
          xmin <- min(sub$students)
          xmax <- max(sub$students)
          pad_x <- max((xmax - xmin) * 0.15, 3)

          # Hug just the step-jump zone itself in the Teacher Salaries panel.
          y_before <- if (xmin > 1) teacher_cum[xmin - 1] else 0
          y_after <- teacher_cum[xmax]
          pad_y <- max((y_after - y_before) * 0.35, teacher_max * 0.02)

          list(
            key = as.character(w),
            panel = "Teacher Salaries",
            cx = (xmin + xmax) / 2,
            cy = (y_before + y_after) / 2,
            rx = (xmax - xmin) / 2 + pad_x,
            ry = (y_after - y_before) / 2 + pad_y,
            label = elem_wave_text[[as.character(w)]]
          )
        })
      )
    } else {
      list()
    }

    c(list(building_region, supplies_region), wave_regions)
  })

  # Elementary tick spacing is finer than the District tab's ($500,000 vs
  # $10,000,000), since one school's costs are naturally a much smaller
  # scale than the whole district's.
  elem_tick_step <- 5e5

  # Back to the same technique used on the District tab: ONE ggplot object,
  # faceted by row with scales = "free_y" AND space = "free_y". ggplot's
  # own layout engine then sizes each row's plotting area exactly
  # proportional to that row's own data range -- trying to reproduce that
  # by hand across four separate plot devices (the previous approach)
  # never quite matched, because it required guessing how many pixels of
  # "chrome" (title/axis/margins) ggplot would actually use. This also
  # restores reliable click handling: Shiny reports which facet row was
  # clicked via `panelvar1`, so hit-testing the ovals works the same way
  # it did when they were separate plots.
  output$elemCostPlot <- renderPlot({
    sim <- elemSim()$trace
    validate(need(
      nrow(sim) > 0,
      "No K-5 students in the current draw yet -- click Refresh."
    ))

    building_cum <- rep(school_cost, nrow(sim))
    supplies_cum <- sim$students * supply_rate
    teacher_cum <- sim$teachers * teacher_cost
    total_cum <- building_cum + supplies_cum + teacher_cum

    shared_breaks <- seq(
      0,
      ceiling(max(total_cum) / elem_tick_step) * elem_tick_step,
      by = elem_tick_step
    )

    long <- rbind(
      data.table(
        students = sim$students,
        ymin = 0,
        ymax = building_cum,
        component = "Building expense",
        panel = "Building Expense"
      ),
      data.table(
        students = sim$students,
        ymin = 0,
        ymax = supplies_cum,
        component = "School supplies",
        panel = "School Supplies"
      ),
      data.table(
        students = sim$students,
        ymin = 0,
        ymax = teacher_cum,
        component = "Teacher salaries",
        panel = "Teacher Salaries"
      ),
      data.table(
        students = sim$students,
        ymin = 0,
        ymax = building_cum,
        component = "Building expense",
        panel = "Total"

  #   - "vertical" circles one jump itself, illustrating that teachers

  #   - "horizontal" circles the flat run BEFORE a jump (the widest one,
  #     for a clear example), illustrating that a step's width isn't
  #     fixed -- it depends on the arrival order of students.
  highWaveRegions <- reactive({
    result <- highSim()
    sim <- result$trace
    if (nrow(sim) == 0) {
      return(list())
    }

    teacher_cum <- sim$teachers * teacher_cost
    teacher_max <- max(teacher_cum)

    jump_at <- which(diff(c(0L, sim$teachers)) > 0)
    if (length(jump_at) == 0) {
      return(list())
    }

    gaps <- diff(c(0L, jump_at)) # width (# students) of the flat run immediately before each jump

    vert_idx <- max(1, ceiling(length(jump_at) / 2))
    vert_pick <- jump_at[vert_idx]

    # The very first jump always happens right at student 1 (even one
    # student is enough to need each subject's first teacher), so it has
    # no real flat run before it -- skip any candidate like that, and
    # skip whichever jump was already picked for the vertical oval, so
    # the two ovals land in visibly different places.
    horiz_order <- order(gaps, decreasing = TRUE)
    horiz_idx <- NA_integer_
    for (idx in horiz_order) {
      if (idx != vert_idx && jump_at[idx] > 1) {
        horiz_idx <- idx
        break
      }
    }
    if (is.na(horiz_idx)) {
      horiz_idx <- horiz_order[1]
    }
    horiz_pick <- jump_at[horiz_idx]
    horiz_gap <- gaps[horiz_idx]

    y_before <- if (vert_pick > 1) teacher_cum[vert_pick - 1] else 0
    y_after <- teacher_cum[vert_pick]
    pad_y <- max((y_after - y_before) * 0.35, teacher_max * 0.02)
    vertical_region <- list(
      key = "vertical",
      panel = "Teacher Salaries",
      cx = vert_pick,
      cy = (y_before + y_after) / 2,
      rx = max(nrow(sim) * 0.012, 1.2),
      ry = (y_after - y_before) / 2 + pad_y,
      label = high_wave_text[["vertical"]]

    xmax <- max(horiz_pick - 1, 1)
    xmin <- max(horiz_pick - horiz_gap, 1)
    if (xmax < xmin) {
      xmax <- xmin
    }
    flat_y <- teacher_cum[xmax]
    pad_x <- max((xmax - xmin) * 0.08, 1.5)
    horizontal_region <- list(
      key = "horizontal",
      panel = "Teacher Salaries",
      cx = (xmin + xmax) / 2,
      cy = flat_y,
      rx = (xmax - xmin) / 2 + pad_x,
      ry = max(teacher_max * 0.025, 1),
      label = high_wave_text[["horizontal"]]
    )

    list(vertical_region, horizontal_region)
  })

  # Modeling Choices tab server logic: fits a straight-line (fixed + rate x
  # students) model to the high school's REAL simulated cost curve (the same
  # highSim() used by the "3. High School" tab), anchored at a chosen
  # starting enrollment, and compares it against the true cost at
  # start + delta. "Fixed" components hold their $ value at the starting
  # enrollment constant across the whole window; "Variable" components use
  # a $/student rate -- supply_rate for Supplies, teacher_cost/teacher_
  # capacity for Teachers (this matches the true model's average teacher
  # cost per student, since teachers arrive in blocks of 6 covering 6
  # sections x 25 students = 150 student-subject-slots, i.e. 25 real
  # students per teacher), and school_cost/high_capacity_per_school for
  # Building (school_cost spread evenly across the school's 1,200-student
  # theoretical capacity).
  ##############################################################################

  output$modelChoicePlot <- renderPlot({
    sim <- highSim()$trace
    start <- input$mc_start
    delta <- input$mc_delta
    end <- start + delta

    validate(need(
      nrow(sim) >= end,
      paste0(
        "The current high school draw only admits ",
        nrow(sim),
        " students -- lower the starting enrollment or change in ",
        "enrollment, or generate a new draw on the \"3. High School\" tab."
      )
    ))

    mc_school_cost <- input$mc_school_cost
    mc_supply_rate <- input$mc_supply_rate
    mc_teacher_cost <- input$mc_teacher_cost
    mc_teacher_capacity <- input$mc_teacher_capacity
    validate(need(
      !is.na(mc_school_cost) &&
        !is.na(mc_supply_rate) &&
        !is.na(mc_teacher_cost) &&
        !is.na(mc_teacher_capacity) &&
        mc_school_cost >= 0 &&
        mc_supply_rate >= 0 &&
        mc_teacher_cost >= 0 &&
        mc_teacher_capacity >= 1,
      "Cost assumptions must be non-negative numbers, and capacity must be at least 1."
    ))

    # The building's total student capacity is built up from the same
    # per-teacher section capacity the user can now edit -- a teacher covers
    # `teacher_classes_per_day` sections, and the school has room for
    # `high_classrooms_per_school / length(subjects)` teachers per subject.
    mc_teacher_student_capacity <- mc_teacher_capacity * teacher_classes_per_day
    mc_high_capacity_per_school <- floor(
      high_classrooms_per_school / length(subjects)
    ) *
      mc_teacher_student_capacity

    building_cum <- rep(mc_school_cost, nrow(sim))
    supplies_cum <- sim$students * mc_supply_rate
    teacher_cum <- sim$teachers * mc_teacher_cost
    total_cum <- building_cum + supplies_cum + teacher_cum

    building_at_start <- idx_or_zero(building_cum, start)
    teacher_at_start <- idx_or_zero(teacher_cum, start)
    true_start <- idx_or_zero(total_cum, start)
    true_end <- idx_or_zero(total_cum, end)

    fixed_part <- 0
    var_rate <- 0
    if (input$mc_supplies_choice == "Variable") {
      var_rate <- var_rate + mc_supply_rate
    } else {
      fixed_part <- fixed_part + mc_supply_rate * start
    }
    if (input$mc_teacher_choice == "Variable") {
      var_rate <- var_rate + mc_teacher_cost / mc_teacher_capacity
    } else {
      fixed_part <- fixed_part + teacher_at_start
    }
    if (input$mc_building_choice == "Variable") {
      var_rate <- var_rate + mc_school_cost / mc_high_capacity_per_school
    } else {
      fixed_part <- fixed_part + building_at_start
    }

    model_end <- fixed_part + var_rate * end
    model_start <- fixed_part + var_rate * start

    # Show the FULL enrollment range the school actually admits (not just a
    # narrow window around start/end), so the start/end comparison is seen
    # in context of the whole staircase. The fit line's slope can run well
    # off the top of that range (especially when a lumpy cost like Building
    # is treated as Variable) -- coord_cartesian() crops the view to the
    # true curve's own range without dropping any of the underlying data,
    # so the line still draws correctly, just partly off-screen.
    # Prepend a (0 students, $0) point so the very first step -- the school
    # opening, its initial 6 teachers, and the first student's supplies, all
    # incurred the instant student #1 arrives -- actually renders as a
    # visible vertical jump at the left edge, instead of the plot's data
    # simply starting mid-air at the row-1 cost.
    full_df <- rbind(
      data.table(students = 0, total = 0),
      data.table(students = sim$students, total = total_cum)
    )

    # Decompose the fit line into its three components, stacked the same
    # order as the real Building/Supplies/Teacher ribbons elsewhere in the
    # app (building at bottom, teachers on top), so the top edge of the
    # stack traces out exactly the same line the single dashed abline used
    # to. Drawn with heavy transparency and a dashed border (rather than
    # the solid fills used for real costs) specifically so it reads as a
    # model, not actual spending.
    model_x <- full_df$students
    building_model <- if (input$mc_building_choice == "Variable") {
      (mc_school_cost / mc_high_capacity_per_school) * model_x
    } else {
      rep(building_at_start, length(model_x))
    }
    supplies_model <- if (input$mc_supplies_choice == "Variable") {
      mc_supply_rate * model_x
    } else {
      rep(mc_supply_rate * start, length(model_x))
    }
    teacher_model <- if (input$mc_teacher_choice == "Variable") {
      (mc_teacher_cost / mc_teacher_capacity) * model_x
    } else {
      rep(teacher_at_start, length(model_x))
    }

    model_long <- rbind(
      data.table(
        students = model_x,
        ymin = 0,
        ymax = building_model,
        component = "Building expense"
      ),
      data.table(
        students = model_x,
        ymin = building_model,
        ymax = building_model + supplies_model,
        component = "School supplies"
      ),
      data.table(
        students = model_x,
        ymin = building_model + supplies_model,
        ymax = building_model + supplies_model + teacher_model,
        component = "Teacher salaries"
      )
    )
    model_long[,
      component := factor(
        component,
        levels = c("Building expense", "School supplies", "Teacher salaries")
      )
    ]

    # The four comparison markers -- true vs. modeled cost, at the current
    # vs. changed enrollment -- are all plotted through a single geom_point
    # layer with `shape` mapped to a factor, so ggplot builds one legend
    # ("key") automatically instead of relying on unlabeled annotate() calls.
    # Everything is drawn in the same red so the shape (open/closed,
    # circle/diamond) is the only thing distinguishing them. Note this
    # deliberately avoids also mapping fill/color here, since those
    # aesthetics are already claimed by the ribbon's Building/Supplies/
    # Teacher scales above -- mapping them again would silently overwrite
    # that scale.
    marker_levels <- c(
      "Modeled cost, current enrollment",
      "Modeled cost, changed enrollment",
      "True cost, current enrollment",
      "True cost, changed enrollment"
    )
    markers <- data.table(
      kind = factor(marker_levels, levels = marker_levels),
      x = c(start, end, start, end),
      y = c(model_start, model_end, true_start, true_end)
    )

    # A solid, reasonably opaque fill with a bold dashed outline keeps the
    # three bands clearly distinct without a busy texture -- the dashed
    # border is the same "this is a model, not real spending" cue used
    # elsewhere in the app (e.g. the old fitted-line style), just applied
    # per band instead of to a single line.
    ggplot(full_df, aes(x = students, y = total)) +
      geom_ribbon(
        data = model_long,
        aes(
          x = students,
          ymin = ymin,
          ymax = ymax,
          fill = component,
          color = component
        ),
        inherit.aes = FALSE,
        alpha = 0.42,
        linewidth = 0.9,
        linetype = "dashed"
      ) +
      scale_fill_manual(
        values = c(
          "Building expense" = palette_cb[["ink"]],
          "School supplies" = palette_cb[["facility"]],
          "Teacher salaries" = palette_cb[["highlow"]]
        ),
        guide = "none"
      ) +
      scale_color_manual(
        values = c(
          "Building expense" = palette_cb[["ink"]],
          "School supplies" = palette_cb[["facility"]],
          "Teacher salaries" = palette_cb[["highlow"]]
        ),
        guide = "none"
      ) +
      geom_step(
        direction = "vh",
        color = palette_cb[["ink"]],
        linewidth = 0.7
      ) +
      # A concave arrow connecting the start and end points directly -- bowed
      # well clear of the true-cost staircase (which sits at or below the
      # straight chord between these two points) so it reads as a distinct
      # "look here" annotation rather than part of the data. Negative
      # curvature bows this particular left-to-right, upward chord above
      # itself -- away from the step line below it -- rather than sagging
      # down toward/through it.
      annotate(
        "segment",
        x = start,
        xend = start,
        y = true_start,
        yend = model_start,
        color = "#D7263D",
        linewidth = 0.9,
        linetype = "dotted"
      ) +
      annotate(
        "segment",
        x = end,
        xend = end,
        y = true_end,
        yend = model_end,
        color = "#D7263D",
        linewidth = 0.9,
        linetype = "dotted"
      ) +
      geom_point(
        data = markers,
        aes(x = x, y = y, shape = kind),
        inherit.aes = FALSE,
        color = "#D7263D",
        size = 3.6,
        stroke = 1.4
      ) +
      scale_shape_manual(
        name = "Markers",
        values = c(
          "Modeled cost, current enrollment" = 5,
          "Modeled cost, changed enrollment" = 18,
          "True cost, current enrollment" = 1,
          "True cost, changed enrollment" = 16
        )
      ) +
      coord_cartesian(
        xlim = c(0, nrow(sim)),
        ylim = c(0, max(total_cum) * 1.12)
      ) +
      scale_x_continuous(labels = comma) +
      scale_y_continuous(labels = comma) +

        title = paste0(

          format(nrow(sim), big.mark = ","),
          " Students)"
        ),
        subtitle = paste0(

          "fitted model, decomposed into Building/Supplies/Teacher components ",
          "at ",
