  ##############################################################################
  # District Cost Implications tab server logic (new): traces total district
  # cost -- elementary + middle + high combined -- across a chosen range of
  # student counts. Uses a vectorized cumulative-count approach (so it scales
  # to a 0-12,000+ student range without an explicit R loop), and decomposes
  # the total into the Building/Supplies/Teacher stacked-ribbon style used on
  # the Elementary and High School tabs, for visual consistency with those.
  ##############################################################################

  districtData <- eventReactive(
    input$district_run,
    {
      min_n <- input$district_range[1]
      max_n <- input$district_range[2]

      validate(
        need(
          max_n > min_n,
          "Maximum must be greater than minimum -- widen the slider range."
        )
      )

      set.seed(input$district_seed)
      draws <- sample(grade_levels, max_n, replace = TRUE)

      # cumulative count of each grade after each of the 1..max_n draws -- used
      # only to know, at every overall step, exactly how far along each band's
      # OWN building trace we are (that band's cumulative headcount so far).
      ind <- sapply(grade_levels, function(g) as.integer(draws == g))
      cum_counts <- apply(ind, 2, cumsum)
      colnames(cum_counts) <- grade_levels

      elem_pos_vec <- rowSums(cum_counts[, elem_grades, drop = FALSE])
      mid_pos_vec <- rowSums(cum_counts[, middle_grades, drop = FALSE])
      high_pos_vec <- rowSums(cum_counts[, high_grades, drop = FALSE])

      # Run each band's own multi-building simulation ONCE, in the actual
      # arrival order (true bin-packing, not a closed-form approximation),
      # then look up each band's state at every overall step.
      elem_trace <- simulate_multi_elem(draws[draws %in% elem_grades])
      mid_trace <- simulate_multi_secondary(
        draws[draws %in% middle_grades],
        middle_grades,
        middle_classrooms_per_school
      )
      high_trace <- simulate_multi_secondary(
        draws[draws %in% high_grades],
        high_grades,
        high_classrooms_per_school
      )

      elem_teachers_vec <- band_lookup(elem_trace, elem_pos_vec, "teachers")
      elem_schools_vec <- band_lookup(elem_trace, elem_pos_vec, "schools")
      mid_teachers_vec <- band_lookup(mid_trace, mid_pos_vec, "teachers")
      mid_schools_vec <- band_lookup(mid_trace, mid_pos_vec, "schools")
      high_teachers_vec <- band_lookup(high_trace, high_pos_vec, "teachers")
      high_schools_vec <- band_lookup(high_trace, high_pos_vec, "schools")

      total_teachers_vec <- elem_teachers_vec +
        mid_teachers_vec +
        high_teachers_vec
      total_schools_vec <- elem_schools_vec + mid_schools_vec + high_schools_vec
      total_students_vec <- seq_len(max_n)

      # Student counts start at 1 in the vectors above, so a minimum of 0 needs
      # a manually prepended all-zero row (an empty district costs nothing).
      idx <- max(min_n, 1):max_n
      if (min_n <= 0) {
        students <- c(0, total_students_vec[idx])
        schools <- c(0, total_schools_vec[idx])
        teachers <- c(0, total_teachers_vec[idx])
        elem_sch <- c(0, elem_schools_vec[idx])
        mid_sch <- c(0, mid_schools_vec[idx])
        high_sch <- c(0, high_schools_vec[idx])
        elem_tch <- c(0, elem_teachers_vec[idx])
        mid_tch <- c(0, mid_teachers_vec[idx])
        high_tch <- c(0, high_teachers_vec[idx])
      } else {
        students <- total_students_vec[idx]
        schools <- total_schools_vec[idx]
        teachers <- total_teachers_vec[idx]
        elem_sch <- elem_schools_vec[idx]
        mid_sch <- mid_schools_vec[idx]
        high_sch <- high_schools_vec[idx]
        elem_tch <- elem_teachers_vec[idx]
        mid_tch <- mid_teachers_vec[idx]
        high_tch <- high_teachers_vec[idx]
      }

      data.table(
        students = students,
        total_schools = schools,
        total_teachers = teachers,
        elem_schools = elem_sch,
        mid_schools = mid_sch,
        high_schools = high_sch,
        elem_teachers = elem_tch,
        mid_teachers = mid_tch,
        high_teachers = high_tch
      )
    },
    ignoreNULL = FALSE,
    ignoreInit = FALSE
  )

  # Two "events" on the Total panel, each shown as a PAIR of ovals joined
  # by an upward arrow: a bottom oval circling the jump on the dark-navy
  # Building Expense band (the actual cause of the jump), and a top oval
  # directly above it -- same x -- circling the resulting jump at the very
  # top of the Total cost curve. Both ovals in a pair share the same `key`
  # and `label`, so clicking either one highlights both and shows the same
  # callout (handled generically by flatten_district_events() below).
  districtSchoolEvents <- reactive({
    dt <- districtData()
    if (nrow(dt) < 2) {
      return(list())
    }

    building_cum <- dt$total_schools * school_cost
    supplies_cum <- dt$students * supply_rate
    teacher_cum <- dt$total_teachers * teacher_cost
    total_cum <- building_cum + supplies_cum + teacher_cum
    total_max <- max(total_cum)

    elem_jump_rows <- which(diff(c(0L, dt$elem_schools)) > 0)
    mid_jump_rows <- which(diff(c(0L, dt$mid_schools)) > 0)
    high_jump_rows <- which(diff(c(0L, dt$high_schools)) > 0)

    events <- list()
    x_pad <- max(diff(range(dt$students)) * 0.03, 40)

    make_event <- function(key, lo_row, hi_row, label) {
      cx <- (dt$students[lo_row] + dt$students[hi_row]) / 2
      rx <- (dt$students[hi_row] - dt$students[lo_row]) / 2 + x_pad

      b_before <- if (lo_row > 1) building_cum[lo_row - 1] else 0
      b_after <- building_cum[hi_row]
      b_cy <- (b_before + b_after) / 2
      b_ry <- (b_after - b_before) /
        2 +
        max((b_after - b_before) * 0.35, school_cost * 0.2)

      t_before <- if (lo_row > 1) total_cum[lo_row - 1] else 0
      t_after <- total_cum[hi_row]
      t_cy <- (t_before + t_after) / 2
      t_ry <- (t_after - t_before) /
        2 +
        max((t_after - t_before) * 0.35, total_max * 0.02)

      # Building cost is often a big fraction of total cost early on, which
      # can make these two ovals' natural sizes overlap -- leaving no room
      # for a sensible arrow between them. Shrink both proportionally
      # (same fraction, so their relative sizes are preserved) whenever
      # that would happen, guaranteeing a visible gap for the arrow.
      gap_needed <- (t_cy - b_cy) * 0.15
      overlap <- (b_cy + b_ry) - (t_cy - t_ry) + gap_needed
      if (overlap > 0 && (b_ry + t_ry) > 0) {
        shrink <- min(overlap / (b_ry + t_ry), 0.9)
        b_ry <- b_ry * (1 - shrink)
        t_ry <- t_ry * (1 - shrink)
      }

      list(
        key = key,
        label = label,
        cx = cx,
        bottom = list(cy = b_cy, rx = rx, ry = b_ry),
        top = list(cy = t_cy, rx = rx, ry = t_ry)
      )
    }

    # (1) One elementary school opening on its own (no coincident middle
    # or high school jump at that same row) -- pick one roughly in the
    # middle of the trace for a clean, clearly-visible example.
    elem_only <- elem_jump_rows[
      !(elem_jump_rows %in% mid_jump_rows) &
        !(elem_jump_rows %in% high_jump_rows)
    ]
    if (length(elem_only) == 0) {
      elem_only <- elem_jump_rows
    }
    if (length(elem_only) > 0) {
      pick <- elem_only[max(1, round(length(elem_only) / 2))]
      events <- c(
        events,
        list(make_event(
          "elem_solo",
          pick,
          pick,
          paste0(
            "New elementary school buildings are expensive enough that total costs ",
            "increase significantly with the opening of a single school (and the hiring ",
            "of a set of 6 grade-level teachers in rapid succession). As a result, the ",
            "overall costs have a distinct sloping staircase feel."
          )
        ))
      )
    }

    # (2) A spot where an elementary, middle, and high school all open
    # within a short span of enrollment (found beyond the very first such
    # cluster, so it's a coincidental later alignment rather than the
    # guaranteed start-of-enrollment one).
    if (
      length(elem_jump_rows) > 0 &&
        length(mid_jump_rows) > 0 &&
        length(high_jump_rows) > 0
    ) {
      first_triple_end <- max(
        elem_jump_rows[1],
        mid_jump_rows[1],
        high_jump_rows[1]
      )
      best <- NULL
      for (e in elem_jump_rows[elem_jump_rows > first_triple_end]) {
        m <- mid_jump_rows[which.min(abs(mid_jump_rows - e))]
        h <- high_jump_rows[which.min(abs(high_jump_rows - e))]
        spread <- max(e, m, h) - min(e, m, h)
        if (is.null(best) || spread < best$spread) {
          best <- list(e = e, m = m, h = h, spread = spread)
        }
      }
      if (!is.null(best)) {
        lo <- min(best$e, best$m, best$h)
        hi <- max(best$e, best$m, best$h)
        events <- c(
          events,
          list(make_event(
            "triple_jump",
            lo,
            hi,
            paste0(
              "The addition of a middle and high school in rapid succession on the heels ",
              "of an elementary school is readily discernible even in the total cost ",
              "roll-up. This produces a staircase pattern at a coarser interval than the ",
              "pattern resulting from the elementary school additions alone."
            )
          ))
        )
      }
    }

    events
  })

  # Unpacks the paired bottom/top event objects above into the flat
  # {key, panel, cx, cy, rx, ry, label} shape the ellipse-drawing and
  # click-hit-testing code expects -- one entry per oval, both tagged
  # with the same `key` (so a hit on either one resolves to the same
  # selection) but a unique `poly_id` (so each draws as its own polygon
  # instead of ggplot trying to connect both into one shape).
  flatten_district_events <- function(events) {
    out <- list()
    for (e in events) {
      out <- c(
        out,
        list(
          list(
            key = e$key,
            panel = "Total",
            poly_id = paste0(e$key, "_bottom"),
            cx = e$cx,
            cy = e$bottom$cy,
            rx = e$bottom$rx,
            ry = e$bottom$ry,
            label = e$label
          ),
          list(
            key = e$key,
            panel = "Total",
            poly_id = paste0(e$key, "_top"),
            cx = e$cx,
            cy = e$top$cy,
            rx = e$top$rx,
            ry = e$top$ry,
            label = e$label
          )
        )
      )
    }
    out
  }

  # Highlight ovals for the Building Expense and Teacher Salaries panels:
  # (1) the first opening of an elementary, middle, AND high school,
  # clustered near the very start of enrollment; (2) the 3rd elementary-
  # school addition, circling both its vertical jump and the flat run
  # that follows it; (3) the next middle- and high-school additions after
  # that, which tend to land close together in enrollment terms; and (4) a
  # patch roughly in the middle of the Teacher Salaries curve, where the
  # many small, staggered per-school hiring jumps blend into what looks
  # like a smooth line at district scale.
  districtBuildingRegions <- reactive({
    dt <- districtData()
    if (nrow(dt) < 2) {
      return(list())
    }

    building_cum <- dt$total_schools * school_cost
    n <- nrow(dt)

    elem_jump_rows <- which(diff(c(0L, dt$elem_schools)) > 0)
    mid_jump_rows <- which(diff(c(0L, dt$mid_schools)) > 0)
    high_jump_rows <- which(diff(c(0L, dt$high_schools)) > 0)
    any_jump_rows <- which(diff(c(0L, dt$total_schools)) > 0)

    regions <- list()

    # (1) First elementary + first middle + first high school together --
    # almost always within the first handful of admitted students.
    if (
      length(elem_jump_rows) > 0 &&
        length(mid_jump_rows) > 0 &&
        length(high_jump_rows) > 0
    ) {
      first_end <- max(elem_jump_rows[1], mid_jump_rows[1], high_jump_rows[1])
      x_pad <- max(diff(range(dt$students)) * 0.035, 35)
      y_after <- building_cum[first_end]
      y_pad <- max(y_after * 0.3, school_cost * 0.2)
      regions <- c(
        regions,
        list(list(
          key = "first3",
          panel = "Building Expense",
          cx = (dt$students[1] + dt$students[first_end]) / 2,
          cy = y_after / 2,
          rx = (dt$students[first_end] - dt$students[1]) / 2 + x_pad,
          ry = y_after / 2 + y_pad,
          label = paste0(
            "The district opens an elementary, middle, and high school as soon as ",
            "the first few students arrive."
          )
        ))
      )
    }

    # (2) The 3rd elementary-school addition -- both the jump and the flat
    # run that follows it, up until the next building of ANY type opens.
    elem3_row <- NA_integer_
    if (length(elem_jump_rows) >= 3) {
      elem3_row <- elem_jump_rows[3]
      y_before <- if (elem3_row > 1) building_cum[elem3_row - 1] else 0
      y_after <- building_cum[elem3_row]

      later_any <- any_jump_rows[any_jump_rows > elem3_row]
      flat_end_row <- if (length(later_any) > 0) later_any[1] - 1 else n

      xmin <- dt$students[elem3_row]
      xmax <- dt$students[max(flat_end_row, elem3_row)]
      x_pad <- max((xmax - xmin) * 0.15, 35)
      y_pad <- max((y_after - y_before) * 0.5, school_cost * 0.2)

      regions <- c(
        regions,
        list(list(
          key = "elem3",
          panel = "Building Expense",
          cx = (xmin + xmax) / 2,
          cy = (y_before + y_after) / 2,
          rx = (xmax - xmin) / 2 + x_pad,
          ry = (y_after - y_before) / 2 + y_pad,
          label = paste0(
            "Elementary schools are added as enrollment grows. The width of these ",
            "steps is wider than the capacity of an elementary school, because as ",
            "new students are enrolled in the district, not all of them go to an ",
            "elementary school."
          )
        ))
      )
    }

    # (3) The next middle- and high-school additions after that.
    after_row <- if (!is.na(elem3_row)) elem3_row else 0L
    next_mid <- mid_jump_rows[mid_jump_rows > after_row][1]
    next_high <- high_jump_rows[high_jump_rows > after_row][1]
    if (!is.na(next_mid) && !is.na(next_high)) {
      first_row <- min(next_mid, next_high)
      second_row <- max(next_mid, next_high)
      y_before <- if (first_row > 1) building_cum[first_row - 1] else 0
      y_after <- building_cum[second_row]

      xmin <- dt$students[first_row]
      xmax <- dt$students[second_row]
      x_pad <- max((xmax - xmin) * 1.2, 100)
      y_pad <- max((y_after - y_before) * 0.5, school_cost * 0.2)

      regions <- c(
        regions,
        list(list(
          key = "midhigh",
          panel = "Building Expense",
          cx = (xmin + xmax) / 2,
          cy = (y_before + y_after) / 2,
          rx = (xmax - xmin) / 2 + x_pad,
          ry = (y_after - y_before) / 2 + y_pad,
          label = paste0(
            "Middle Schools and High Schools are added at roughly the same cadence. ",
            "Even though middle schools only have on average 75% of the capacity of ",
            "high schools, they only have to serve 3 grades (as opposed to 4 in high ",
            "school). This means they fill to capacity at roughly the same rate."
          )
        ))
      )
    }

    # (4) A patch roughly in the middle of the Teacher Salaries curve.
    teacher_cum <- dt$total_teachers * teacher_cost
    mid_row <- max(1, round(n / 2))
    x_pad <- max(diff(range(dt$students)) * 0.06, 40) * 3
    y_pad <- max(max(teacher_cum) * 0.05, teacher_cost * 0.5) * 3
    regions <- c(
      regions,
      list(list(
        key = "teacher_smooth",
        panel = "Teacher Salaries",
        cx = dt$students[mid_row],
        cy = teacher_cum[mid_row],
        rx = x_pad,
        ry = y_pad,
        label = paste0(
          "While teachers are added in discrete steps, looking at things on a ",
          "district scale makes the costs associated with teachers seem like a ",
          "smoother, almost linear function of students. This is in part because ",
          "the addition of teachers at multiple schools simultaneously do not line ",
          "up with each other. Additionally, the cost of each teacher is a small ",
          "jump of overall district costs."
        )
      ))
    )

    regions
  })

  output$districtCostPlot <- renderPlot({
    dt <- districtData()
    validate(need(
      nrow(dt) > 0,
      "No data to show -- click Trace District Costs."
    ))

    building_cum <- dt$total_schools * school_cost
    supplies_cum <- dt$students * supply_rate
    teacher_cum <- dt$total_teachers * teacher_cost
    total_cum <- building_cum + supplies_cum + teacher_cum
    total_max <- max(total_cum)

    tick_step <- 1e7
    shared_breaks <- seq(
      0,
      ceiling(total_max / tick_step) * tick_step,
      by = tick_step
    )

    # One panel per row: Building, Supplies, Teacher (each a single solid-
    # color ribbon), then Total (the same three, stacked) at the bottom.
    # This is ONE ggplot object faceted by row, with scales = "free_y" AND
    # space = "free_y" -- ggplot's own layout engine then sizes each row's
    # PLOTTING AREA exactly proportional to that row's own data range,
    # correctly separating that from the (small, shared, consistent) strip
    # label and axis chrome. That's what a manual grid.arrange of separate
    # ggplot objects can't guarantee, since each one's title/margins eat a
    # fixed amount of space regardless of how tall its row is assigned to
    # be -- this is why School Supplies looked disproportionately short
    # before. The shared $10,000,000 tick spacing still applies everywhere;
    # a small-range row like Supplies just ends up showing fewer of them.
    long <- rbind(
      data.table(
        students = dt$students,
        ymin = 0,
        ymax = building_cum,
        component = "Building expense",
        panel = "Building Expense"
      ),
      data.table(
        students = dt$students,
        ymin = 0,
        ymax = supplies_cum,
        component = "School supplies",
        panel = "School Supplies"
      ),
      data.table(
        students = dt$students,
        ymin = 0,
        ymax = teacher_cum,
        component = "Teacher salaries",
        panel = "Teacher Salaries"
      ),
      data.table(
        students = dt$students,
        ymin = 0,
        ymax = building_cum,
        component = "Building expense",
        panel = "Total"
      ),
      data.table(
        students = dt$students,
        ymin = building_cum,
        ymax = building_cum + supplies_cum,
        component = "School supplies",
        panel = "Total"
      ),
      data.table(
        students = dt$students,
        ymin = building_cum + supplies_cum,
        ymax = total_cum,
        component = "Teacher salaries",
        panel = "Total"
      )
    )
    long[,
      component := factor(
        component,
        levels = c("Building expense", "School supplies", "Teacher salaries")
      )
    ]
    long[,
      panel := factor(
        panel,
        levels = c(
          "Building Expense",
          "School Supplies",
          "Teacher Salaries",
          "Total"
        )
      )
    ]

    # Highlight ovals: the paired bottom/top "a new school opens" ovals on
    # the Total row, plus the Building Expense callouts. Whichever KEY
    # matches the current click selection is drawn in solid red with a
    # thicker outline -- since both ovals in a Total pair share one key,
    # clicking either highlights both -- same technique as the Elementary
    # and High School tabs otherwise.
    events <- districtSchoolEvents()
    regions <- c(flatten_district_events(events), districtBuildingRegions())
    selected_key <- if (!is.null(districtSelected())) {
      districtSelected()$key
    } else {
      NULL
    }
    ellipse_layers <- NULL
    if (length(regions) > 0) {
      theta <- seq(0, 2 * pi, length.out = 100)
      ellipse_df <- rbindlist(lapply(regions, function(r) {
        poly_id <- if (is.null(r$poly_id)) r$key else r$poly_id
        data.table(
          x = r$cx + r$rx * cos(theta),
          y = r$cy + r$ry * sin(theta),
          region_id = poly_id,
          panel = factor(r$panel, levels = levels(long$panel)),
          selected = identical(r$key, selected_key)
        )
      }))
      ellipse_layers <- list(
        geom_polygon(
          data = ellipse_df,
          aes(
            x = x,
            y = y,
            group = region_id,
            color = selected,
            linewidth = selected,
            linetype = selected
          ),
          inherit.aes = FALSE,
          fill = "white",
          alpha = 0.32
        ),
        scale_color_manual(
          values = c(`TRUE` = "#D7263D", `FALSE` = palette_cb[["ink"]]),
          guide = "none"
        ),
        scale_linewidth_manual(
          values = c(`TRUE` = 2.2, `FALSE` = 0.9),
          guide = "none"
        ),
        scale_linetype_manual(
          values = c(`TRUE` = "solid", `FALSE` = "dashed"),
          guide = "none"
        )
      )
    }

    # Arrows connecting each Total-panel event's bottom oval (on the dark
    # navy Building Expense band) up to its top oval (on the total cost
    # curve), showing that the jump at the bottom shows up at the top too.
    # Colored via the same `selected` mapping/scale as the ovals, so the
    # arrow turns red along with its pair when either oval is clicked.
    arrow_layer <- NULL
    if (length(events) > 0) {
      arrow_df <- rbindlist(lapply(events, function(e) {
        y_from <- e$bottom$cy + e$bottom$ry
        y_to <- e$top$cy - e$top$ry
        data.table(
          x = e$cx,
          xend = e$cx,
          y = y_from,
          yend = max(y_to, y_from + 1),
          panel = factor("Total", levels = levels(long$panel)),
          selected = identical(e$key, selected_key)
        )
      }))
      arrow_layer <- geom_segment(
        data = arrow_df,
        aes(x = x, xend = xend, y = y, yend = yend, color = selected),
        inherit.aes = FALSE,
        linewidth = 0.8,
        arrow = arrow(length = unit(0.2, "cm"), type = "closed")
      )
    }

    ggplot(
      long,
      aes(x = students, ymin = ymin, ymax = ymax, fill = component)
    ) +
      geom_ribbon() +
      {
        if (!is.null(ellipse_layers)) ellipse_layers
      } +
      {
        if (!is.null(arrow_layer)) arrow_layer
      } +
      scale_fill_manual(
        values = c(
          "Building expense" = palette_cb[["ink"]],
          "School supplies" = palette_cb[["facility"]],
          "Teacher salaries" = palette_cb[["highlow"]]
        )
      ) +
      facet_grid(
        rows = vars(panel),
        scales = "free_y",
        space = "free_y",
        labeller = labeller(panel = label_wrap_gen(10))
      ) +
      scale_x_continuous(labels = comma) +
      scale_y_continuous(labels = comma, breaks = shared_breaks) +
      labs(
        title = paste0(
          "Cost Buildup for the Whole District (seed = ",
          input$district_seed,
          ")"
        ),
        x = "Students Enrolled",
        y = "Cost ($)",
        fill = "Cost Component"
      ) +
      theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
      theme(
        legend.position = "top",
        strip.text.y = element_text(face = "bold", angle = 0),
        panel.spacing = unit(1.4, "lines")
      )
  })

  districtSelected <- reactiveVal(NULL)

  observeEvent(input$districtPlotClick, {
    click <- input$districtPlotClick
    clicked_panel <- click$panelvar1
    hit <- NULL
    if (!is.null(clicked_panel)) {
      all_regions <- c(
        flatten_district_events(districtSchoolEvents()),
        districtBuildingRegions()
      )
      for (r in Filter(function(r) r$panel == clicked_panel, all_regions)) {
        in_oval <- ((click$x - r$cx) / r$rx)^2 + ((click$y - r$cy) / r$ry)^2 <=
          1
        if (isTRUE(in_oval)) {
          hit <- r
          break
        }
      }
    }
    districtSelected(hit)
  })

  observeEvent(districtData(), {
    districtSelected(NULL)
  })

  # Right-hand column, same layout technique as Elementary/High School: one
  # block per facet row, weighted by that row's own peak dollar value. The
  # district's ovals live on the Building Expense, Teacher Salaries, and
  # Total rows, so those are the only blocks that ever show a callout.
  output$districtNotesColumn <- renderUI({
    dt <- districtData()
    if (nrow(dt) == 0) {
      return(NULL)
    }

    w_building <- max(dt$total_schools * school_cost)
    w_supplies <- max(dt$students * supply_rate)
    w_teacher <- max(dt$total_teachers * teacher_cost)
    w_total <- w_building + w_supplies + w_teacher

    sel <- districtSelected()
    note_block <- function(r) {
      if (is.null(r)) {
        return(NULL)
      }
      div(
        class = "situation-card",
        style = "font-size: 13px; line-height: 1.5;",
        HTML(r$label)
      )
    }
    building_note <- if (!is.null(sel) && sel$panel == "Building Expense") {
      note_block(sel)
    } else {
      NULL
    }
    teacher_note <- if (!is.null(sel) && sel$panel == "Teacher Salaries") {
      note_block(sel)
    } else {
      NULL
    }
    total_note <- if (!is.null(sel) && sel$panel == "Total") {
      note_block(sel)
    } else {
      NULL
    }

    header_spacer_px <- 70

    div(
      style = "display: flex; flex-direction: column; height: 900px;",
      div(style = paste0("height: ", header_spacer_px, "px; flex: none;")),
      div(
        style = paste0(
          "flex: ",
          w_building,
          " 1 0; min-height: 110px; display: flex; align-items: center; padding: 4px;"
        ),
        building_note
      ),
      div(style = paste0("flex: ", w_supplies, " 1 0;")),
      div(
        style = paste0(
          "flex: ",
          w_teacher,
          " 1 0; min-height: 110px; display: flex; align-items: center; padding: 4px;"
        ),
        teacher_note
      ),
      div(
        style = paste0(
          "flex: ",
          w_total,
          " 1 0; min-height: 110px; display: flex; align-items: center; padding: 4px;"
        ),
        total_note
      )
    )
  })

  output$districtCostSummary <- renderUI({
    dt <- districtData()
    last <- dt[nrow(dt)]

    total_cost <- last$total_schools *
      school_cost +
      last$students * supply_rate +
      last$total_teachers * teacher_cost

    HTML(paste0(
      "<div style='font-size:15px; line-height:1.7;'>",
      "<b>At ",
      format(last$students, big.mark = ","),
      " students:</b><br>",
      "Elementary: ",
      last$elem_schools,
      " school(s), ",
      last$elem_teachers,
      " teachers<br>",
      "Middle: ",
      last$mid_schools,
      " school(s), ",
      last$mid_teachers,
      " teachers<br>",
      "High: ",
      last$high_schools,
      " school(s), ",
      last$high_teachers,
      " teachers<br><br>",
      "<b>Total schools:</b> ",
      last$total_schools,
      "    <b>Total teachers:</b> ",
      last$total_teachers,
      "<br>",
      "<b>Total cost at that enrollment:</b> $",
      format(round(total_cost), big.mark = ","),
      "</div>"
    ))
  })
}

# School District Cost Model Explorer -- Setup Instructions

This is a single-file R Shiny app (`SchoolDistrictCostModelApp.R`) for the school
district cost-modeling case. No other files are needed to run it.

## 1. Requirements

- R (any recent version) and RStudio.
- Four packages: `shiny`, `ggplot2`, `data.table`, `scales`.

If you don't already have these installed, run once in the R console:

```r
install.packages(c("shiny", "ggplot2", "data.table", "scales"))
```

## 2. Running the app

1. Save `SchoolDistrictCostModelApp.R` into its own folder (any folder is fine).
2. Open that file in RStudio.
3. Click the **Run App** button in the top-right of the script editor pane
   (or run `shiny::runApp()` from the console with that folder as your
   working directory).

## 3. Heads-up on the first launch

Tab 7 ("Assessing Model Fit") runs 1,000 simulated district enrollment
patterns to compare a cost model against reality. That computation is the
slowest thing the app does.

- **First launch:** expect a delay of roughly 1-2 minutes while this runs.
- **Every launch after that:** near-instant. The app saves the results to a
  small file, `model_fit_cache.rds`, in the same folder as the script, and
  reuses it automatically as long as the file is still there.

You don't need to do anything to enable this -- it's automatic. If your
folder happens to be read-only, the app will just recompute it every time
(slower, but it won't break anything).

## 4. Notes

- Everything is self-contained in the one `.R` file -- no external data
  files, no hardcoded folder paths. It should run identically on any
  machine with R/RStudio and the four packages above.
- If you ever want a completely fresh recompute of the Tab 7 simulation
  (e.g., after editing the model), just delete `model_fit_cache.rds` and
  relaunch -- it will regenerate automatically.
